newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha gains ground, backwardation steeper.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha gains ground, backwardation steeper.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices jumped in afternoon trade on Thursday, tracking crude gains on the ACCESS after-hours trading system, traders said.
They also said tight availability in the physical market added to naphtha's strength.
Bids for first-half February open-spec naphtha were heard at $237.00, while offers were notionally assessed at $238.50. It was indicated at about $234.00/236.00 in late trading on Wednesday.
Second-half February was quoted at $234.00/235.50, up from Wednesday's $229.00/231.00.
Backwardation in inter-month naphtha spreads broadened further, with first-half February/first-half March discussed at plus $6.00/7.00, compared to Wednesday's plus $5.50/6.50.
The outlook for a tighter supply/demand balance in Asia in 1997 led backwardation to continue widening, traders said.
Major ethylene plants are scheduled to come on-stream next year in India, Singapore and Thailand, boosting the region's naphtha demand substantially.
Naphtha supplies in Asia, on the other hand, are expected to remain virtually unchanged, traders said.
